report:
Reviewed the complete narrow_detail claim, six ordinary implementation entries, the implementation TODO in ty.rs, and the sole TODO test. Requirements: field details and associated-item enumeration are separately keyed from the owner signature; selecting an associated item obtains that item's signature without eagerly checking siblings; enumeration does not check sibling signatures or bodies.

Ordinary implementation: LocalStructSym::fields is a distinct tracked query from sig. sig computes the generic binder and declared parameter environment without lowering fields. fields reopens the signature's parameters and lowers field types in its own output stash. The present field detail product groups the owner's fields; the claim requires separation from the owner signature and does not promise a separate query for every individual field. LocalTraitSym::items and LocalImplSym::items are separate tracked queries from their sig methods, passing existing owner parameters to associated::lower_items. lower_items walks member kind/name/occurrence keys, obtains symbols through keyed trait/impl associated-item queries and returns TraitItemDef handles in a binder. It does not call member signature or body queries. local_associated_items supplies an additional identity-only membership boundary through tracked trait/impl enumeration helpers, without even requiring the owner signature. Keyed member lowering copies selected CST and creates the corresponding function/type/constant symbol; copying syntax is not checking its body or signature.

LocalFnSym::sig is keyed by the selected function symbol. It opens its owner's signature for generics/Self/predicates, then checks the selected function's own declaration. Owner signatures do not enumerate or check sibling methods. This does not prohibit the owner's binder or legitimate type/trait interfaces required by the selected declaration. The captured generic checker, type syntax checker, predicate lowering and Check completion helpers support that path without adding eager sibling function signature/body queries. BinderExt in the initial ty.rs implementation file iterates existing parameters, so enumeration and details reuse the owner binder instead of rebuilding parameters. Whole associated.rs also shows the shared key-based lowering boundary, including functions, types and constants.

Implementation deferral is material: the ty.rs TODO explicitly says associated type aliases and constants lack checked signature queries and requires item-keyed APIs that reuse the owner binder without eager sibling checking. Captured type_aliases.rs and consts.rs confirm these types currently supply symbols/CST/attributes rather than such checked signature operations. Their selection/signature portion is therefore not claimed implemented. The existing narrow associated-type-value normalization helper in impls.rs is not treated as a replacement for a complete associated type signature API.

Test evidence remains deferred. todo::checking_signature_narrow_detail contains only the explicit verification matrix comment, not behavioral assertions. It calls for query traces selecting a field or associated item, rejecting unselected sibling signatures and all bodies, and persistent edits that preserve owner binder identity and unrelated detail queries. The prerequisite for missing item kinds is the signature APIs identified in the implementation TODO. For existing field/function/enumeration paths, completing the matrix requires source-backed query observation and persistent database edits with meaningful identity and execution comparisons. This TODO honestly retains the full verification gap; passing the placeholder would not establish any of those behaviors. No N/A evidence applies and no new suspected defect was identified requiring a reproduction.

Executed a fresh cargo meta review start with coordinator instructions and review read captures for checking design, signature/type/generic/predicate helpers, and the currently limited type-alias/constant symbol APIs. Assessed current source and the complete associated test. No test commands or build were run by this reviewer; central suite results are separate. No source edits. Recorded assessment retains both existing implementation and test TODOs rather than claiming full implementation or verification.
